claims.text: Adding approximately 0.5 at.% Si to a refractory high-entropy alloy will promote formation of a continuous, adherent silicide/silica surface scale.
The Si-induced surface scale will slow oxidation relative to the untreated alloy.
A Mo-Nb-Re-Ta-W refractory high-entropy alloy without Si can serve as the baseline alloy.
The proposed oxidation-resistance improvement should occur at approximately 1200 °C in an oxygen-rich atmosphere near 1 atm for approximately 100 hours.
The Si-enriched alloy surface will form a thin, continuous silicide/silica layer.
The silicide/silica layer will act as a barrier to oxygen diffusion.
At high temperature, the minor Si addition will diffuse to the alloy surface.
Surface Si will react during oxygen exposure to produce stable silicides and subsequently a silica layer.
The protective scale will reduce oxygen ingress into the alloy.
The Si-modified alloy will exhibit lower oxidation weight gain than the untreated alloy.
The Si-modified alloy will develop a thinner oxide scale than the untreated alloy.
The Si-modified alloy will develop a more adherent oxide scale than the untreated alloy.
The Si-modified alloy will exhibit delayed degradation relative to the untreated alloy.
The untreated refractory high-entropy alloy is expected to form thicker, less protective oxide scales under high-temperature oxidizing conditions.
Excessive Si additions might cause embrittlement or unwanted phase formation.
Different oxygen pressures or higher temperatures may alter scale adherence.

contradictions.description: The operating conditions describe an oxygen-rich atmosphere at roughly 1 atm, whereas the experiment specifies air. If 1 atm refers to oxygen partial pressure, air provides only about 0.21 atm oxygen; the pressure basis is therefore inconsistent or ambiguous.
